heading: Make room for your best work.
intro: A capable assistant for the calendar, inbox, documents and follow-ups that fill your day. Build a practical role around the work you need off your desk.
serviceHeading: More help. Less on your plate.
statement: Your time belongs to the work only you can do.
body: The rescheduled meeting. The unanswered supplier. The document that still needs finishing. Together, the small things become a full-time job. Give them a dedicated person, clear instructions and a reliable place to land.
contactTitle: What would make your week easier?

services.title: Executive Calendar Management
services.summary: Keep meetings, focus time and scheduling requests organized.
services.imageAlt: Office professional checking a folder beside her laptop
tasks: Review new meeting requests against working hours, focus blocks, and travel time
Draft calendar updates with the right title, guests, links, notes, and time zone
Prepare a short conflict list for the executive or manager to decide
Send approved reminders and keep a daily note of open scheduling questions
controls: Use delegated calendar access instead of sharing the executive's password
Keep board, legal, medical, investor, and personal meetings private unless access is approved
Require owner approval before declining requests, moving priority meetings, or promising availability
launch: Share the current calendar, preferred meeting hours, focus blocks, and three examples of a good invite
Have the assistant prepare changes in a review list without moving or declining meetings
Review conflicts together, approve the safe changes, and write down every new exception rule
